newsitem.title: THAILAND: Burma military junta detains Suu Kyi associates.
newsitem.headline: Burma military junta detains Suu Kyi associates.

text.p: At least five close associates of Burmese opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi have been detained by the ruling military for allegedly smuggling her videotaped speeches abroad, opposition sources said on Friday.

The ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) was upset when pressure groups outside the country received and used a smuggled, videotaped speech by Suu Kyi opposing Burma's membership of the Asociation of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), they told Reuters.
ASEAN groups Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, Philippines, Thailand, Brunei and Vietnam. It agreed to accept Burma as a new member in late July despite Suu Kyi's opposition.
Among those held included her relatives and her personal photographer, a source from Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy (NLD) said.
There was no SLORC comment on the opposition claim.

Cho Aung Than, a cousin of the Nobel Peace laureate, was picked up for interrogation last Friday, while his sister and her husband were arrested a few days later on the same charge, the NLD source added.
Photographer Ko Sunny and Hon Myint, an aging politician who is related to Suu Kyi, were arrested two days ago.
"They interrogated Ko Sunny on what kind of pictures he took and how he managed to ship some video out of the country," a close Suu Kyi aide said.
The NLD source blamed ASEAN for the new round of detentions.
"ASEAN will have to bear full responsibility for this because they accepted Burma into the grouping and that does activists nothing but disservice in Burma," the source said.
Suu Kyi has said that if Burma became an ASEAN member it would give the ruling junta a licence to repress the opposition movement and suppress human rights further in the country.
